review.tagline: Native Rust CLI that lets AI agents drive Chrome via accessibility snapshots
review.summary: agent-browser is a Rust command-line tool that controls Chrome for AI agents. It exposes an accessibility-tree snapshot with element refs (@e1, @e2) that commands like click, fill and get text can target, alongside CSS and semantic locators. It also covers screenshots, network interception, HAR recording, cookies, batch execution, an optional MCP profile and experimental WebMCP support.
review.audience: Developers giving AI agents scriptable browser control from the shell
strengths: Snapshot refs let agents target elements without writing selectors
Native Rust binary; daemon needs no Playwright or Node.js
Batch mode runs multiple commands in one process invocation
Detects existing Chrome, Brave, Playwright and Puppeteer installs
weaknesses: Requires downloading Chrome via a separate install step
Linux needs extra system libraries via install --with-deps
Refs go stale after page changes and need a fresh snapshot
needs: Needs Chrome (Chrome for Testing), Node.js 24+ and pnpm 11+ (source build only), Rust (source build only)
